the development of new computational methods for the prediction of free energies of solvation and binding.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CM3 atomic charges are not better than EPS charges, but that CM3 charges are better than CM1 charges for absolute free energies of hydration.

the CM1 and especially the CM3 charges, with appropriate scaling factors, are useful for the computation of free energies of solvation of organic molecules, but the CM1A charges are superior to the CM3A ones.
the scaled CM1 charges yield the best overall results for the set of molecules studied here, and that the CM1 charges are superior to the CM3 charges for this set of molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now in a position to compute the free energies of hydration of small organic molecules to an accuracy of about ± 1 kcal/mol.

the CM1A and CM3A charges are not significantly more accurate than charges obtained from the electrostatic potential, but that the scaling factors determined for the CM1A charges are transferable to other molecules.
the scaled CM3A charges are the most accurate for the full set, while the scaled CM1A charge set is the best for amides and for the subset of molecules in the original work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CM1 and the CM3 partial charges are not as good as the EPS charges for computing absolute free energies of hydration.
the best charges for organic compounds are those that are derived from the electrostatic potential (ESP) of ab initio calculations, not charges derived from semiempirical methods.
the CM1 and the CM3 charges are not superior to charges fit to the EPS for the calculation of hydration free energies, but they can be improved by scaling by 1.10–1.15.
